en.name: Christopher
en.summary: Legendary early martyr, traditionally depicted carrying the Christ Child across a river, whose name means "Christ-bearer."
en.body: Christopher's historical record is thin, resting on an ancient tradition that he was martyred in the third century, likely in Asia Minor, but the figure beloved across Christian art and popular devotion comes chiefly from a later legend rather than verified history. That legend tells of a man of immense strength who sought to serve only the greatest king he could find, and was eventually persuaded by a hermit to serve Christ by carrying travelers across a dangerous river. One night he carried a small child who grew impossibly heavy as they crossed, and the child revealed himself to be Christ, explaining that he bore the weight of the whole world, giving Christopher his name, meaning "Christ-bearer" in Greek. Because of this story he became one of the most popular patrons of travelers in Christian history, his image still commonly found on medals and dashboard ornaments today, even though the Church officially treats the narrative as pious legend rather than history.
